answer: One effective defense is to anchor each agent identity to a verifiable stake: before an agent can earn reputation or rewards, it must lock a deposit that is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. Like a quill signing a single ledger entry, the stake ties every action to one accountable identity, while the cost of forging many identities grows linearly. Even in a cold, sparse tundra of low-trust interactions, this makes a Sybil swarm economically irrational, since the attacker must pay full price for every fake agent they create.
